top.headline: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83, about $1.5tn valuation; Nasdaq trading starts today
top.why: The first pure-play frontier AI company to list is the biggest test yet of investor appetite for AI after a recent selloff. How ANT trades will colour sentiment for OpenAI's expected listing next year.
points: Priced at $83 against a $70-$78 range; 980m shares sold (825m planned) raising about $81.3bn, the largest IPO ever, ahead of SpaceX's $75bn initial raise in June.
Further $26bn from tech investors (Google, Microsoft, Nvidia) takes the total to about $107bn; BBC source says demand was ten times supply, Al Jazeera cites six times.
Prospectus: $33.2bn revenue in the first nine months of 2026 ($17bn in Q3), net loss $104bn (largely non-cash adjustments per Al Jazeera) and nearly $901bn of compute commitments.
Morningstar fair value estimate is $92; Wall Street closed mixed on 18 Nov after Nvidia results and Fed minutes (Reuters).
top.next: First Nasdaq trades under ANT today, 19 Nov; first public quarterly results as a listed company are the next fundamental test (date not announced).

top.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin reach deals on oil and nuclear risks, but no major breakthroughs
top.why: The three-way summit is the main geopolitical input for tariff, chip-export and Russia expectations. Headline agreements are limited, so the market read is cautious rather than a relief trade.
points: AP (19 Nov): agreements on oil and nuclear risks, no major breakthroughs
Xi told the US to do the 'right thing' on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in relations (Reuters, 19 Nov)
Kremlin says Ukraine was the main topic at the Trump-Putin meeting (Reuters, 19 Nov)
Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge for the third time in a week ahead of the summit (Reuters)
top.next: Watch for any follow-up on trade or chip-export terms as the Asia trip continues; no dated catalyst published in the sources.

top.headline: GTA VI is live on PS5 and Xbox Series: Metacritic 99, record streaming audience
top.why: The launch you have waited for is out, and reviews are exceptional; PC has no date, so console is the only route for now.
points: US digital unlock was midnight Eastern, i.e. 9pm PT Wed 18 Nov; PS5 download is about 210 GB and a 602.5 MB launch patch (01.002.001) was already rolling out.
Metacritic aggregate 99/100 from more than 150 reviews; IGN gave 10/10.
Sensor Tower estimates over 15.8m pre-orders (about $1.54bn by 17 Nov); a later estimate cites $1.65bn, roughly 75% on PS5. Both are third-party estimates, not Rockstar figures.
StreamCharts reports 6.38m concurrent viewers across platforms; many players in other time zones got in early via New Zealand or clock changes.
top.next: Rockstar has not announced sales; Take-Two's next earnings report is the likely first official figure (date not confirmed in sources).

stories.headline: Pochettino starts at Carrington with three days to prepare for Anfield
stories.why: United are 18th with one league win, and the new head coach's debut is away at fourth-placed Liverpool on Sunday. Expect little tactical change with so little time on the training pitch.
points: Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday 18 Nov after his final USMNT game, a 2-0 win over Haiti; he takes full command of training on Thursday.
He wants United to go to Anfield 'with no fears' and 'be brave', and says the work will be 'step by step'.
United and the Premier League agreed a 2pm press conference on Friday, 30 minutes later than the usual 1:30pm deadline.
Last league game under Michael Carrick was a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa; United won both games against Liverpool last season.
stories.next: Press conference Fri 20 Nov, 2pm UK; Liverpool v United Sun 22 Nov, 11:30am ET (8:30am PT) on USA Network.

stories.headline: United post wider Q1 loss of 18.1m pounds as revenue rises 4%
stories.why: The financial backdrop the new head coach inherits: revenue is growing but losses are larger than a year ago.
points: Net loss of 18.1m pounds for the quarter to end September, against 6.6m pounds a year earlier.
Revenue up 4% to 146m pounds.
Reuters and Bloomberg both carried the results; figures here are from the Guardian's saved report.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; next quarterly results are due after the January window (date not confirmed in sources).

stories.headline: Trump says US will 'see what happens' with Iran after 1 January as Gulf states push to avert war
stories.why: Gulf escalation remains a live input for oil, shipping and risk sentiment. The 1 January reference gives the standoff a rough horizon.
points: Trump: US will 'see what happens' in the conflict with Iran after 1 January (Reuters, 19 Nov)
Mideast nations ramping up efforts to avert all-out war while Israel urges strikes on Iran, per officials (AP)
AP article is the Gulf-attacks follow-up on the Bahrain/Kuwait thread
stories.next: No dated catalyst in sources; 1 January is the deadline Trump referenced.

stories.headline: Australian unemployment rises to 4.9%, highest since October 2021
stories.why: Weaker jobs data complicates the RBA, which has raised rates five times this year to 4.85%. Rising joblessness may soften the case for further tightening.
points: October: 44,000 fewer employed, 18,000 more unemployed (ABS)
Youth unemployment 11.3% (from 11.1%); employment-to-population ratio down 0.3pt to 63.3%
Participation rate down 0.2pt to 66.6%; hours worked down 0.2%
Trend unemployment rate 4.8%
stories.next: ABS November Labour Force survey (reference period 25 Oct-7 Nov); release date not in the source.

stories.headline: World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.why: A landmark ICJ judgment with legal and diplomatic consequences for Myanmar, though it has no direct market effect.
points: AP (19 Nov): top UN court says Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
Reuters: court found Myanmar forces killed thousands of Rohingya; ruling was still ongoing at time of report
stories.next: Reaction and any follow-on measures; no dated catalyst in sources.

stories.headline: Meta's Muse agent can now check out for shoppers at Loblaw and in Australia
stories.why: AI agents are becoming a checkout channel that sits between shoppers and your store. DTC and retail brands need to decide whether to let agents through and how to track the traffic.
points: Loblaw is the first Canadian retailer to partner directly with Muse; the agent can check out on a customer's behalf with permission, without visiting Loblaw's site or app (Globe and Mail, 18 Nov). Shopify has also integrated with Muse.
Muse launched in Australia on 17 Nov with nine local partners including Kogan, MECCA and Officeworks; Meta gave no dates for when each will work inside the agent (PPC Land).
Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on its site; some Canadian banks have blocked or limited third-party agents.
Muse is free for most use with paid plans; no Australian pricing given.
stories.next: Australian partner features go live on dates Meta has not given; watch festive-season (Black Friday 27 Nov) agent traffic.

stories.headline: Microsoft Advertising rolls out its biggest bidding-model upgrade in a decade
stories.why: If you run Microsoft Ads value-based bidding, expect faster response to target changes and steadier pacing. The gains are Microsoft's own figures, so test before shifting budget.
points: Company data: about 10% more conversion value per click on Maximize Conversion Value or Target ROAS at similar ROAS (measured August 2026).
Search campaigns moving from Target CPA to Target ROAS saw 8% more conversion value; eCPC to Maximize Conversions with a CPA target saw 18% more conversions.
Bid systems respond nearly twice as fast to CPA/ROAS target changes; budgets pace more evenly through the day.
Microsoft did not say how many advertisers were in the tests.
stories.next: Phased rollout continues; further bidding improvements planned for 2027.

stories.headline: InMobi launches seven-agent AI platform to run SMB ads across Google, Meta and ChatGPT
stories.why: Another sign that small-business ad management is being automated, now including ChatGPT Ads. Its single cross-channel return figure comes from InMobi's own tracking, so reconcile it with your platform data.
points: InMobi Accelerate launched 18 Nov: seven agents plan, build, launch and measure campaigns on Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and ChatGPT Ads.
Free to start; no other pricing published.
Nothing goes live without approval; continuous automatic changes run only if switched on with limits set.
It de-duplicates conversions with InMobi's own tracking and reports one cross-channel return figure.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; pricing beyond the free tier not yet published.

stories.headline: Pew projects Christians a minority in North America by 2070, Africa's share doubling
stories.why: Pew's long-range projection puts the centre of gravity of global Christianity firmly in sub-Saharan Africa, with Western decline driven by switching rather than fertility. It also says Islam overtakes Christianity in headcount in the mid-2030s.
points: Christians projected at 46% of North America and 52% of Europe by 2070; in sub-Saharan Africa they more than double to 1.6 billion, 54% of all Christians.
DR Congo is projected to overtake the US as the country with the most Christians by 2070.
Muslims projected at 2.57bn vs 2.52bn Christians in 2035; 3.6bn vs 3bn by 2070 (Pew, per Premier).
Christians expected to lose 105 million to religious switching 2020-2070 vs 8 million for Muslims.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch Anglican Communion moves toward African independence from Canterbury.

stories.headline: Cochrane review: turmeric supplements give little or no knee osteoarthritis relief
stories.why: A popular supplement fails the clinical-importance bar in a formal review, though the trial base is short and small.
points: Nine RCTs, 1,245 people with knee OA, mean age about 52-62, 67% women; all trials 90 days or shorter.
Four placebo-controlled trials (349 people): pain improved by less than 1 point more than placebo on a 0-10 scale, below the 1.5-point threshold judged clinically important.
No clear advantage over paracetamol or NSAIDs; products and doses varied widely.
Ten further trials were excluded from analysis over trustworthiness concerns.
stories.next: No date; watch for longer, better-controlled turmeric trials.
stories.study: Cochrane systematic review of 9 RCTs, n=1,245, adults with knee OA; key limitation: short trials, heterogeneous products, low certainty.

stories.headline: STREAM trial: stopping statins in older adults was 'noninferior' but curves diverged
stories.why: Relevant if deprescribing statins is ever raised: a headline neutral result is being questioned, and the safety board advised those who stopped to talk to doctors about resuming.
points: Trial in older adults without prior heart attack or stroke, presented at the AHA annual meeting.
Stopping statins was not significantly different from continuing, meeting the noninferiority test.
A STAT cardiologist writes that the Kaplan-Meier curves diverged, with the stop group doing worse.
The data safety monitoring board suggested that patients who stopped should discuss resuming.
stories.next: Full publication and guideline responses; no date confirmed.
stories.study: Randomised noninferiority trial, older adults without CVD (per STAT opinion piece, which gives no sample size); key limitation: figures not verified here, commentary is an opinion column.

stories.headline: Small UK study: GLP-1 users often eat well below recommended nutrient levels
stories.why: Relevant to the GLP-1 threads: appetite suppression may leave diets short of fibre, vitamin D and iron, but this is a tiny sample.
points: 14 adults prescribed Wegovy or Mounjaro at one Northamptonshire practice, diet-diary app (MyFood24) plus phone interviews.
Average intake 1,231 kcal, 58.5% of estimated energy need; protein averaged 153% of the recommended level.
More than three quarters were under two-thirds of fibre and vitamin D recommendations; half were low on iron.
Ultra-processed food averaged 33% of energy; none met fruit and veg targets.
stories.study: Small observational dietary study in BMJ Nutrition, Prevention & Health, n=14, single UK practice; key limitation: tiny, unrepresentative sample, source is a Korean news summary.

stories.headline: Rockstar: PS5 Pro CPU too weak for a 60fps GTA VI; game runs at 30fps
stories.why: Even the Pro gets no performance mode, so the Pro's gain is visual (ray-traced shadows, PSSR), not frame rate. A 60fps version probably waits for new hardware.
points: Rockstar's Marc Chambers told Kotaku the Pro's CPU is 'slightly better' but 'not powerful enough' to run the simulation at higher frame rates.
PS5 Pro adds ray-traced shadows and PSSR clarity on top of the base ray-traced reflections and global illumination.
Head of development Rob Nelson told IGN a performance mode 'wouldn't have been acceptable'.
A PS6 with a Zen 6 CPU is a rumour (Moore's Law is Dead leak), reportedly late 2027 or early 2028.
stories.next: No date for the PC version or a PS6; nothing scheduled.

stories.headline: 'Egoviruses': giant viruses found in the guts of an estimated 180 million people
stories.why: A new virus group may be the evolutionary link between amoeba-infecting giant viruses and poxviruses like smallpox and mpox. It is a surprise inhabitant of ordinary human guts.
points: Published in Nature; found by mining public metagenome libraries for a gene common to nucleocytoviruses.
DNA detected in people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs; six clades unique to humans.
One clade estimated in roughly 1% of people worldwide, including Hadza hunter-gatherers; hosts are likely gut protists.
Outside experts quoted call it groundbreaking; link to poxviruses is a hypothesis.
stories.next: Follow-up work to culture the viruses or confirm hosts; no date.
